news.title: US ELT hit by 14% student drop and shorter stays
news.summary_en: The number of students on English language programs in the US declined by 14% in 2025, as experts highlight the knock-on impact on higher education and communities across the country.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: The PIE Live Asia Pacific 2026: Insights from Julian Hill MP
news.summary_en: Speaking at The PIE Live Asia Pacific, Hill tackles social licence and market concentration, warning that when 60–70% of students come from one country it’s bad for student experience, social licence, soft power and business risk. He also points to recent government action including the suspension of new VET/ELICOS entrants and and argues that the sector has largely backed these measures.
news.author: The PIE News team

news.title: Watch as Tracy Harris picks up the lifetime impact award at The PIE Live Asia Pacific
news.summary_en: Tracy Harris, principal of Tracy Harris Solutions, was honoured with the lifetime impact award at this week's PIE Live Australia Pacific, held on Australia's Gold Coast.
news.author: The PIE News team

news.title: Japan and Russia resume youth exchanges
news.summary_en: A youth exchange program between Japan and Russia is set to resume next month after a seven-year hiatus.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Most NOSCs stay flat as Australia releases 2027 provider numbers
news.summary_en: Australia has published indicative provider-level allocations for 2027, with public universities largely retaining their previous allocations while other higher education providers receive recalculated allocations under a revised methodology.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Beechside views: six people universities need to understand in Burnham’s Britain
news.summary_en: As Andy Burnham settles into No. 10, Diana Beech outlines the movers and shakers in his cabinet that UK universities should get to know.
news.author: Diana Beech

news.title: India reforms exams after protests force minister’s resignation
news.summary_en: New legislation, tougher penalties for exam malpractice and a wider review of India's examination system form the Modi government's biggest response yet to the NEET-UG crisis, though organisers warn the protest movement is far from over.
news.author: Abhishek Nair
